title: Sketching and describing qualitative graphs
keyIdea: A graph without numbers can still tell a story: rising, falling, flat, steeper or levelling off.

kid: You can draw a graph from a story, even with no numbers. 'I ran to the bus stop' is a steep line going up.
'I waited' is a flat line. 'The bus took me home fast' is a steep line going back down.
adult: Match each part of a story to a shape. Steady change is a straight line. Faster change is steeper. No change is flat. Change that slows down is a curve that levels off.
When you describe a graph, use words like increasing, decreasing, constant, steeper and levelling off. Always say what the axes stand for.

familyTip: Tell a short story about a trip, then each person sketches it. Compare the sketches.

practice.prompt: A flat line on a distance–time graph means…
practice.explain: No change in distance: standing still.

practice.prompt: Walk for {a} min, then wait for {b} min. For how many minutes is the graph flat?
Walk {a} km in {t} min, then rest. How far from home is the flat part, in km?
A hot drink cooling quickly, then more slowly. The temperature graph…

pool.prompt: Running to the bus stop, then waiting, looks like…
pool.explain: Distance rises fast, then stays the same.

pool.prompt: A line sloping back down to zero distance from home means…
Filling a bath, the water depth graph rises then is flat. The flat part means…
pool.explain: Depth stays the same, so the tap is off.

pool.prompt: A plant's height rises fast, then levels off. Describe it.
pool.explain: It grows quickly at first, then hardly at all.

pool.prompt: Walk {a} min, wait {b} min, walk {c} min. How many minutes long is the graph?
Walk {a} km at a steady pace in {t} min. What is the gradient, in km per min?
Which story matches 'rises steadily, flat, then rises more gently'?
pool.explain: Second walking part is less steep, so slower.

visual.caption: Run to the bus stop, wait, then ride the bus. Play the story and watch each part of the graph.
